chapter_theme: Songs at Madurantakam (மதுராந்தகம்), at its northern Chirrambalam: the poet asks to cling to the feet as a raft instead of the leaking body, asks to be taught the instruction Murugan once gave Siva, and asks to leave house, kin and wealth for the vastness of silence.

718.reading: The poet asks that he not tire and whirl taking as everything this hut of the senses, skin and holes from which blood spurts and drains, packed with deeds, a vessel of filth, but that he be given the thought to hold the raft of the twin lotus feet with golden bells and anklets. The praise names Murugan nephew of the cloud-dark one who bears mace, Sarnga bow, sword, conch and discus, bridegroom of the cane-sweet girl of the millet field, born in the lotus as the son of the destroyer of Kama, lord of the northern Chirrambalam at Madurantakam.
718.nuance: உபய அம்புயப் புணை: the feet as a raft across the sea of births, an image the Kural also uses (kural:10). குணபாண்டம் is perhaps 'corpse-vessel' (குணபம், corpse). The line உதித அம்பரத்தை உயிர் கெட is obscure to me.

719.reading: The poet asks whether Murugan's guruship would be diminished in the least if he spoke to him, small as he is, the instruction he gave Siva, who gave the mountain-daughter his left side and keeps the Ganga in his hair, so that Siva's speech ended, his action died, his mind loosened and he attained the eternal. The praise names the vel that split the mango in the sea so the gods might live, the blue peacock that circled the whole universe in an instant, and the one who broke the ancient golden hill, at Madurantakam.
719.nuance: The teaching of Siva is described by its effect, not named as Om: உரைமாள, செயல் மாண்டு, சித்தம் அவிழ, நித்தத்துவம் பெற. The plea is witty: சற்றும் குருத்துவம் குறையுமோ, would it cost the guru anything to teach the poet too? கொக்கு is the mango tree that Sura became.

720.reading: The poet seems to ask when, leaving house, sons, kin, horses, grain, wealth and town and the delusion of 'I and mine', he will be taken into the vast silence and given Murugan's feet. The praise, much of it in drum syllables, names Siva who dances in space, whose child Murugan is, the elephant-faced brother with the mouse, the six-faced lord of Madurantakam honoured by the gods.
720.nuance: யானெனதென்று: the plea names the 'I and mine' that binds, and மோன தடம்பர the expanse of silence that replaces it. The song is set to a dense rhythm, and most compounds in both halves (வணவாம்பிர மாத குணங்குறி, இடவார்ந்தன சானு) can be split several ways, so this reading is only the outline.

links.note: Both make the Lord's feet the way across the sea of births: the Kural says only those who join his feet swim it, and 718 calls the twin lotus feet a raft (புணை) to be grasped instead of the leaking body.

718 calls the body a hut of the senses made of skin and holes from which blood drains (குருதி வடி தொளைத் தொக்கு இந்த்ரியக் குரம்பை) and asks not to take it as everything. Naladiyar 42 sees the same body as full of holes under a skin covering (தோல்போர்வை மேலும் தொளைபலவாய்) that hides its falsity. Both make skin and openings the body's truth; the Naladiyar asks for a changed view, the song for the feet as a raft away from it.

719 describes the teaching Murugan gave Siva by its effect: speech ended, action died, the mind loosened (உரைமாளச் செயல்மாண்டு சித்தம் அவிழ). Tirumanthiram 1896 defines silence as speech and mind both still (வாக்கு மனமும் இரண்டும் மவுனமாம்), not the tongue alone. The song's upadesa produces exactly the double stilling the Tirumanthiram calls மவுனம், which the poet then asks for himself.

720 asks to leave house, sons, wealth and town together with the delusion of 'I and mine' (யானெனதென்று) and be taken into the expanse of silence. Kural 346 says one who cuts the pride of saying I and mine (யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு) enters a world above the gods'. The song uses the Kural's very pair and names what replaces it: மோன தடம்.
